name: Boubyan Bank
founded: 2004 (incorporated 21 Sep 2004 under Amiri Decree No. 88; CBK licence 28 Nov 2004; listed 15 May 2006)
ownership_summary: Listed on Boursa Kuwait since 15 May 2006. National Bank of Kuwait is the parent and the only holder above 5%, with 60.368% at 31 Dec 2025 (Boubyan AR 2025); NBK reports 60.4% (NBK AR 2025; 2Q 2026 presentation). A Boubyan-Gulf Bank merger study was called off on 14 Jan 2025.
government_link: No direct government holding above 5% disclosed; controlled by NBK (60.4%), which has no controlling shareholder.
group_structure: Boubyan Bank K.S.C.P. (listed) is a 60.4% subsidiary of National Bank of Kuwait (kw-nbk), which consolidates it in full - NBK's group assets, deposits and profit already include Boubyan, so never add the two. Boubyan's principal subsidiaries: Boubyan Capital Investment Company K.S.C. (Closed) (100%, Islamic investments - asset management, alternatives, brokerage); Boubyan Takaful Insurance Company (98.88%); BLME Holdings (72.37%; 27.63% non-controlling), owner of Bank of London and The Middle East plc (UK), which trades as Nomo (Islamic digital bank) and owns BLME Capital Company (Riyadh). Boubyan Capital and BLME are not profiled separately; their details are recorded here.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Boubyan is a fully Shariah-compliant group whose stated wealth strategy is to 'maximize wealth management growth ... through Boubyan Capital, BLME, and NOMO Bank' and to create 'distinctive Islamic wealth management opportunities' (6M 2026 presentation). In Kuwait, wealth is led by CEO Consumer, Private & Digital Banking Abdullah Al-Tuwaijri (also Chairman of Boubyan Capital) with an invitation-only Private Banking proposition; Boubyan Capital (100%, CMA-regulated, est. 2007) runs three in-house funds, discretionary/non-discretionary portfolios, custody, alternatives (international real estate, private debt, co-investments) and a Shariah-compliant brokerage platform covering 19 markets (Chinese market added 2025). Boubyan Capital launched the Boubyan Invest robo-advisory platform in March 2021 (min USD 5,000); its current status is unclear. Internationally, 72.4%-owned BLME offers UK property-led private banking and, through its digital bank Nomo, Nomo Investments: three discretionary Shariah portfolios (Cautious/Balanced/Adventurous) from USD 1,000, 1.00% annual fee, delivered with Allfunds' Nextportfolio (partnership publicised Sep 2026), with growing demand from Kuwait and UAE customers. BLME Capital (Riyadh, launched May 2023) serves KSA HNW clients. No group AUM figure is disclosed; fiduciary assets were KD 1.15bn at 31 Dec 2025.

brokerage.detail: Boubyan Capital Shariah-compliant brokerage: one account for 19 markets (Kuwait, GCC, KSA, Egypt, USA incl. OTC, Europe/LSE via CHIX, China, Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea), sukuk trading, mobile app, desktop app and 'Brokerage Pro'; Chinese market added and trading platform upgraded in 2025.

digital_investing.detail: Boubyan Capital brokerage app; Boubyan Invest digital investment platform (launched 17 Mar 2021, goal/risk-based portfolios, min USD 5,000; current status unclear); Nomo app (UK) with Nomo Investments portfolios. The Boubyan (Kuwait) app's investments page lists deposits, three Boubyan Capital funds and brokerage only.

advisory.detail: Boubyan Capital provides advisory and portfolio services; Boubyan Invest includes a 'digital investment advisor' with human advisors on request.

discretionary.detail: Boubyan Capital discretionary portfolio management; Nomo Investments are discretionary managed portfolios (FSCS-covered UK entity).

model_portfolios_robo.detail: Nomo Cautious (25% equities/75% cash and sukuk), Balanced (50/50) and Adventurous (75/25) portfolios selected via in-app investor personality questionnaire; Boubyan Invest robo-advisory (2021).

funds_platform.detail: Nomo Investments built with Allfunds' Nextportfolio digital investment solution (Allfunds also offers fund distribution and model portfolios). Boubyan Capital occasionally distributes funds managed by other investment companies (e.g. US equipment-leasing Ijara funds).

structured_products.detail: No structured notes/products found; Boubyan Capital's 'structured leasing' items are closed-ended Ijara funds, not structured products.

BLME real estate investments.

islamic_wealth.detail: Entire group is Shariah-compliant: Shariah-screened brokerage lists by market, sukuk trading, Shariah funds, Nomo Shariah portfolios (equities + sukuk).
